key_insight: EP-Flow reframes disordered crystal prediction as generating a physically valid occupancy distribution matrix, enabling disorder modeling without site-level annotations.
engineering_relevance: This matters for designing functional materials with vacancy, substitutional, or interstitial disorder when only the chemical formula is known.
method: Represents disorder with an Occupancy Distribution Matrix (ODM) that unifies ordered and disordered crystals.
Canonicalizes formula-dependent transportation polytopes into a shared double-centered space for learning.
Uses Entropic Polytope Flow with a Sinkhorn inverse map to recover feasible occupancies while jointly predicting coordinates and lattice parameters.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art results on formula-conditioned disordered crystal structure prediction benchmarks derived from COD and MPDS, with improved recovery of sparse, chemically meaningful local disorder.
watch_item: The approach depends on solving constrained transport and Sinkhorn-based inversion, which may add computational overhead and sensitivity to optimization stability.
paper_title: EP-Flow: Disordered Crystal Structure Prediction without Site-Level Annotations
